notes: ADR 0002 leaves the spring weight to M1, decided by hand before anything is built. If taken, SW1-n drops by 4. Mixed weights cost nothing but a second line on the same order

2k2. The 10k this started at was fine for a register beside its switch, and the 2k2 was chosen when the node ran 265mm down an UNCOATED loom - that reason is gone now the register is back on the cluster board. Kept anyway as cheap insurance: the cavity is still breathed into for hours at 10-20K above ambient and the switch contacts are still open, and 1.5mA per PRESSED key against a 360mA budget is nothing. TWENTY-FOUR: one per switch position including the 3 spare-switch bits, PLUS one each for the 3 genuinely free bits (22, 23, 31) which the first cluster-board draft left floating - the exact ADR 0001 fix-6 fault, and unretrofittable

description: Series resistor between each switch and its 74x165 input
notes: With C-KEY: press crosses V_IL at key-press-time so it stays instant, and release crosses V_IH at key-release-time, which is a free hardware debounce. SUPERSEDED: this field carried ~1us and ~93us, both computed on the 10k/10nF network that is no longer fitted - the network is 2k2/47nF. Also bounds injected current

description: Filter cap at each 74x165 key input
notes: 47nF with the 2k2 pull-up keeps tau at ~103us. Press crosses the HC165's VIL (0.99V at 3.3V) within key-press-time - see that figure for the margin against the 250us scan period - and release crosses VIH (2.31V) at key-release-time. *** DO NOT JUSTIFY THIS PART BY THE COUPLING ARGUMENT: IT IS WRONG (see ADR 0001). *** A capacitive divider cannot exceed the aggressor's swing, and on the real 5V data line an unfiltered wire sees 1.36V, which does not cross a 0.8V threshold. The filter is cheap insurance and a BOUNCE filter; it is not the thing that makes the topology safe
